incidents.vector: External Microsoft Teams accounts posing as IT help desk placed voice-phishing calls to coerce employees into running remote-access tools or custom malware, in some cases escalating to NTLM relay attacks against domain controllers.
incidents.impact: More than 150 employees across at least 10 organizations were targeted between January and April 2026; successful calls delivered remote-control tooling and obfuscated payloads aimed at domain-level compromise.

incidents.vector: Facebook and Instagram ads disguised as adult content lured users into downloading malware apps that steal banking credentials.
incidents.impact: Meta removed dozens of fraudulent ads after India flagged the pattern; India recorded nearly $2.4 billion in cyber-fraud losses in 2025, with scam operators increasingly targeting banking customers.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised an unnamed third-party application connected to McKesson systems and are actively exfiltrating data.
incidents.impact: Customers face intermittent service degradation at a company that delivers roughly one-third of all North American prescriptions; a prolific extortion group claimed credit and is threatening to leak stolen data. Disclosed in an SEC filing.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion into two Berlin state ministries between August 7-12, with data stolen before the breach was discovered mid-August.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim 5.79 TB of government data including contracts, emails, passwords and classified material, auctioned for roughly $2.3 million; Berlin refuses to pay. Two ministries were cut off from the state network, disrupting public services weeks before September 20 elections.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on systems used to process and ship customer orders; intrusion method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Global operations of the medical device maker (nearly 60,000 employees) were disrupted, affecting order processing and shipping. Disclosed to the SEC.

incidents.victim: Philippine Nuclear Agency and naval contractor
incidents.vector: Network intrusions into the Philippine nuclear research agency and a major naval contractor; details not yet public.
incidents.impact: Suspected Chinese state hackers breached sensitive government and defense-industrial networks amid regional tensions in the South China Sea.

incidents.vector: Compromised websites display fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA overlays that trick users into pasting malicious PowerShell into Windows Terminal, leading to DLL sideloading and payloads hidden in PNG images.
incidents.impact: Infected hosts receive a reverse-tunnel implant giving attackers persistent network-level proxy access, plus extensive Active Directory reconnaissance — a staging position for ransomware and data theft.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
incidents.vector: Ransomware group breached one standalone system at the agency; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The agency confirmed the incident but says its main network was unaffected and public portals remain operational.

incidents.vector: Data theft followed by a $3.3 million ransom demand, which the company refused.
incidents.impact: Data of nearly 13 million customers was published online after the refused extortion attempt; the dataset also contained millions of synthetic fake records.

incidents.vector: Data theft from airport WiFi sign-up systems followed by an extortion demand, which the company refused.
incidents.impact: Data of 8.7 million travelers who passed through Manchester, East Midlands and London Stansted airports was stolen, including email addresses used for airport WiFi registration.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion into the systems of a SCADA software provider serving US water utilities, followed by a failed extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: Company data was leaked after the extortion failed; the incident raises supply-chain concerns for water utilities using its SCADA products, though it is unrelated to recent Iranian attacks on the sector.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack in mid-July on the book distribution platform managed by Hachette Australia; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Six weeks later the distribution platform is still not restored, leaving some Australian bookstores running out of stock.

incidents.victim: Government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain and Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures deployed a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Campaigns from September 2025 through April 2026 established initial access for intelligence collection against European diplomatic targets, including activity tied to Moldova's parliamentary elections; higher-value targets received a more responsive second-stage implant.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem and thousands of downstream businesses
incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm embedded in compromised open-source libraries (including Trivy, KICS, LiteLLM and Telnyx) stole developer credentials and spread to other packages.
incidents.impact: Australian police arrested two alleged members of the group behind the longest-running software supply-chain attack spree on record — over 500,000 stolen credentials, cloud secrets harvested from 2,500+ organizations, and extortion of major companies. Both suspects remain in custody.

incidents.victim: US federal agencies incl. NASA, Federal Reserve, DOE, DOJ, HHS, NIH, US Senate
incidents.vector: A China-based contractor operated a scanning platform that mass-infected internet-of-things devices worldwide, chaining them into an obfuscation network that disguised the origin of intrusions against US networks.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized the hard-coded domains, rendering both hacking platforms inoperable and disrupting a service sold to China's Ministry of State Security and military. Activity dated back to at least 2018.

incidents.victim: Academia, defense, government and think-tank personnel (US and Europe)
incidents.vector: Three distinct clusters abuse legitimate authentication flows — app-password phishing, OAuth consent phishing, and Microsoft/WhatsApp device-code phishing — often impersonating the US State Department or diplomatic conferences.
incidents.impact: Persistent, highly targeted account-takeover campaigns against individuals of interest to Russia; compromised accounts grant attackers mailbox and messaging access without triggering two-factor authentication.

incidents.victim: Web servers in government, education, media, tech and gaming sectors globally
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing Windows and Linux web servers, accelerated by AI-generated exploit scripts and playbooks, followed by privilege escalation and custom cross-platform implants.
incidents.impact: Compromised servers across Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam were monetized through SEO fraud and data theft; a target list of roughly 170,000 URLs and a new implant with kernel-level EDR-killing and Linux rootkit capabilities indicate an ongoing, scaled operation.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure PLC operators (manufacturing, energy, water, chemical)
incidents.vector: Internet scanning to find exposed Siemens S7-series PLCs, then AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to gain read/write access to controller memory and logic.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of active reconnaissance and pre-positioning against US industrial control systems that could enable disruption of critical processes, safety incidents and equipment damage.

incidents.vector: Rebranded Russian-made traffic speed cameras shipped with a built-in backdoor granting shell and network access via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers.
incidents.impact: Slovakia's security service flagged 279 cameras bought under a €30 million EU-funded project; deployment is paused pending an independent audit, and similar devices may be installed in Croatia and elsewhere in Eastern Europe.

incidents.victim: 144 US universities, 178 foreign universities, companies and agencies
incidents.vector: Sustained spearphishing campaign against more than 100,000 professor accounts to steal credentials and harvest academic research at scale.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment charging 17 members of an Iran-based hacking-for-hire institute that stole over 31 terabytes of research and intellectual property for the IRGC; the State Department is offering up to $10 million for information on five defendants.

incidents.victim: 1,100+ companies in software, staffing, healthcare and finance
incidents.vector: Covert IT workers using at least 22 fabricated personas, AI-generated photos and real-time AI interview assistance applied to remote technical jobs at scale, supported by facilitators hosting company laptops.
incidents.impact: Operators were likely employed at ten or more organizations, funneling salaries to the North Korean regime and creating insider-threat exposure including recorded internal meetings and access from personal devices.
